title: The 5 Biggest Power Plants on Earth, Ranked (None Burns Anything)

scenes.text: The five biggest power plants on Earth. Not one of them burns anything.

scenes.label: Belo Monte · 11.2 GW
scenes.text: Number five: Belo Monte in Brazil. About eleven gigawatts, built on the Xingu River.

scenes.label: Xiluodu · 13.9 GW
scenes.text: Number four: Xiluodu in China. About fourteen gigawatts, on the Jinsha River.

scenes.label: Itaipu · 14 GW
scenes.text: Number three: Itaipu, shared by Brazil and Paraguay. Exactly fourteen gigawatts, from one river.

scenes.label: Baihetan · 16 GW
scenes.text: Number two: Baihetan in China. Sixteen gigawatts, a giant that is only a few years old.

scenes.label: Three Gorges · 22.5 GW
scenes.text: Number one: the Three Gorges Dam in China. Twenty-two and a half gigawatts, more than double any nuclear plant.

description:
The five biggest power plants on Earth, ranked by installed capacity.
All five are hydroelectric dams, and the biggest nuclear plant doesn't make the list.
Which would you have guessed was number one?
first_comment: Did you expect zero nuclear plants on this list? Which record should we rank next?
